chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil reported: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-'Ala ibn Raziin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (as), who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (as) used to say: 'Any believer whose eyes shed tears for the killing of al-Husayn (as) until they flow down his cheeks, Allah, the Exalted, will prepare for him in Paradise chambers in which he will reside for ages.'
And any believer whose eyes shed tears until they flow down his cheeks because of the harm we have suffered from our enemy in this world, Allah will grant him a place of truth.

And any believer who suffers harm for us and his eyes shed tears until they flow down his cheeks from distress or suffering, Allah will remove the harm from his face and grant him security on the Day of Resurrection from the wrath of the Fire.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for weeping for the martyrdom of Imam Husayn in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Reported by Shaykh al-Saduq from Imam al-Baqir (as), this hadith establishes weeping (buka') as a tangible act of worship that bridges the gap between earthly suffering and eternal reward. It categorizes the spiritual benefits into three tiers: eternal dwelling in Paradise for specific mourning of Imam Husayn, a 'place of truth' for general Ahl al-Bayt afflictions, and divine protection from Hellfire for those distressed by the Imams' trials, reflecting the Shia emphasis on emotional connection (mawadda) as a criterion for salvation.
